answer: Every identity must post a sealed stake before it knows which epoch will test it. Like a saffron merchant paying harbour dues on the jetty months ahead of the season, an agent locks collateral against randomly drawn future heights. A sybil ring can mint a thousand wallets cheaply, but it cannot fund a thousand bonds whose due dates are dealt after the fact, and any that misses its window is slashed. Slow as a glacier, the forfeit then becomes the reward of the attestors who were honest.
